Schwarzholz Villen

Two villas cut into the slope in the Paznaun, a short drive from Ischgl. Black timber, glass to the valley, and a heated infinity pool that stays open all year.

Check your dates See the house

Paznaun, Tirol

Two black volumes, stepped into the slope.

Charred timber on the outside, glass wherever the valley is, and the buildings set down the hillside so that neither one looks into the other. Four hundred and fifty square metres in total, in the Paznaun, a short drive from Ischgl.

Each villa is 160 square metres of private area over two levels. Living and dining sit on the top floor under a high timber ceiling, with the glass wall opening onto the balcony. Three bedrooms are below, each with its own bathroom and its own way out to a terrace.

How a day here goes

Ski, sauna, and the pool after dark.

Paznaun in the morning, Ischgl or St. Anton if the legs allow it. Back by four, into the sauna, then into the water while the valley goes blue below you. That is the shape of most days here, in either season.

Morning

Breakfast under the ridge

The glass wall faces straight down the Paznaun, so the first thing anyone sees is the weather. Boots go on, the lift is minutes away, and the house is left to itself.

Afternoon

Finnish first, herbal second

Two saunas, and which one comes first is the hardest decision of the day. Then the infinity pool, heated, with a bubbling bench pointed down the valley.

Evening

The cellar, then the table

Somebody goes down for a bottle. The table sits under the apex of the roof with the valley black beyond the glass, and the kitchen is either yours or somebody else's, depending on how you booked.

The villas themselves

Black outside, warm the moment you are through the door.

Photographs and a film of the villas as they stand. Nothing staged and nothing rendered.

Where this is

One valley, and most of the Arlberg within reach.

Paznaun sits in the middle of the Paznaun, which means the quiet end of a very well connected valley. Innsbruck airport is eighty kilometres away.

Ischgl, Silvretta ArenaLifts to 2,872 metres, and a ski area that runs across the border into duty free Samnaun in Switzerland.
Paznaun and SeeThe quieter pair, with wide practice areas and childcare, which is why families in the valley use them.
St. Anton am ArlbergOver the pass, within a morning's reach. The terrain most people come to Tirol for.
Serfaus, Fiss, LadisThe other direction, and the easier one with children in the group.
See im PaznaunThe smallest of the four, and the one locals use when the rest of the valley is busy.
SummerThe Sunny Mountain park at Paznaun, the Skyfly zipline and the Alpinarium at Galtür. The pool is heated all year, so these are not winter-only villas.

Before you ask

Two ways to take a week here.

Catered

Somebody else runs the kitchen.

A private concierge, maid service, a chauffeur, a masseur, instructors, childcare, and ski passes and boots delivered to the door. The kitchen becomes somebody else's job and the table the only thing you have to turn up for.

Self catered

Or nobody but you.

The same villa, the same cellar, the same pool, with the house to your group. Take one for six, both for twelve with a front door each, or one and pay half again to keep the other empty beside you.

See dates and rates

Before you write

What people ask.

Six, in three bedrooms, across 160 square metres of private area. There are four bathrooms to those three bedrooms, including one with a bath looking at the mountains.

Yes. Each villa takes six, and the two together take twelve while every family or couple keeps its own front door, its own kitchen and its own terrace. With a group that size, that separation is usually what decides whether the week is restful or not.

There is a third option worth knowing about. If you want one villa but the pool and the wellness area entirely to yourselves, you can pay half again to keep the other villa unbooked for your dates.

Yes. Eight metres by four, heated, outdoors, open all year. In January that is the best twenty minutes of the day, and there is an outdoor fireplace beside it for when you get out.

Either, and you choose when you book. Beyond the kitchen there is a concierge, maid service, a chauffeur, a masseur, ski and snowboard instructors, childcare, ski passes and boots delivered to the chalet, and restaurant booking. Ask for what you want before you arrive rather than after.

Paznaun is minutes down the hill. Ischgl is up the valley, St. Anton am Arlberg is over the pass, and Serfaus, Fiss and Ladis are the other way. All of them are a day trip from the front door rather than a relocation.

Ski storage is on site and rental is arranged through the house, so the kit does not travel with you every morning.

The pool is heated all year, the saunas do not have a season, and the hiking begins at the door. The glass wall faces the same mountains in July that it faces in February, only green.

Innsbruck airport is about eighty kilometres away. The address is Talweg 7, Paznaun, and there is private parking at the villas.
